theme: 3 terms on attributes: words with an at sign that inform the compiler, ignoring a return value, and marking which versions can use code

terms.definition: A word that starts with an at sign and gives the compiler extra information about a declaration.
terms.example: Add the `@escaping` Attribute, because we store the closure.

terms.definition: An attribute, written `@discardableResult`, that lets callers ignore a function's return value without a warning.
terms.example: Mark `add` with Discardable Result, since most callers don't need the count.

terms.definition: An attribute, written `@available`, that says which versions can use a declaration or that it is deprecated.
terms.example: I added an Availability Attribute, so `fetch()` now shows a rename warning.

video.title: Attribute, Discardable Result & Availability Attribute | Day 54
video.description:
Learn to explain Swift attributes: Attribute, Discardable Result & Availability Attribute, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Attribute - A word that starts with an at sign and gives the compiler extra information about a declaration.
Discardable Result - An attribute, written `@discardableResult`, that lets callers ignore a function's return value without a warning.
Availability Attribute - An attribute, written `@available`, that says which versions can use a declaration or that it is deprecated.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

landscape.title: Swift Attribute, Discardable Result & Availability Attribute | Day 54
landscape.description:
Explain Attribute, Discardable Result & Availability Attribute in Swift by listening to a real code chat between two iOS devs.
속성, 버릴 수 있는 결과, 가용성 속성 표현을 영어 대화로 익혀요.

Attribute - A word that starts with an at sign and gives the compiler extra information about a declaration.
한국어: 속성: @ 기호로 시작해 선언에 대한 추가 정보를 컴파일러에 알려 주는 단어

Discardable Result - An attribute, written `@discardableResult`, that lets callers ignore a function's return value without a warning.
한국어: 버릴 수 있는 결과: @discardableResult로 쓰며, 함수의 반환값을 무시해도 경고가 나지 않게 하는 속성

Availability Attribute - An attribute, written `@available`, that says which versions can use a declaration or that it is deprecated.
한국어: 가용성 속성: @available로 쓰며, 어떤 버전에서 선언을 쓸 수 있는지나 더 이상 권장되지 않음을 알려 주는 속성

In this video, Mina and Jake sort out why a function shows a yellow warning, why ignoring a return value is allowed and what words with an at sign are, in a chat-style conversation, with the Swift code on screen.
Mina와 Jake의 채팅 스타일 대화와 화면 속 Swift 코드로 배워요.

landscape.hook: Can you explain Swift attributes in English?

dialogue.title: Why the yellow warning?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, Xcode shows a yellow warning on `store()`. Did I break something?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: No, I added an Availability Attribute. It marks `store()` as deprecated.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. The Availability Attribute even says `save` is the new name.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: OK. But `save` returns a `Bool`, and I ignore it. Why no warning?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: It has Discardable Result on top, so ignoring it is fine.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Isn't that risky? What if saving fails?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Fair point. Use Discardable Result only when the value is just extra info.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So every word with an at sign is an Attribute?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Pretty much. An Attribute gives the compiler extra information.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Got it. Availability Attribute for versions, Discardable Result for ignored values.
An Attribute starts with an at sign.
